query: What topics are covered in CSE202 Object Oriented Programming?
supplied_context_sample:

2. OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING IN C++ by E BALAGURUSAMY, MCGRAW HILL

List of Practicals / Exper...
answer:
The topics covered in CSE202: Object Oriented Programming include:

- Concepts and Basics of C++ Programming: Introduction to OOP, reading/writing data using cin and cout, creating classes, access to class members, differences between structures, unions, enumerations, and classes, inline and non-inline member functions, static data members and functions, procedural vs object-oriented programming paradigms, input/output streams [[cite:8ad84b89037231bb]].

- Functions: Functions with default parameters, inline functions, manipulators, function overloading, scope rules, friend functions and classes, differences between call by value, call by address, and call by reference, recursion [[cite:8ad84b89037231bb]].

- Pointers, Reference Variables, Arrays and String Concepts: Void pointers, pointer arithmetic, pointer to pointer, dangling and wild pointers, null pointer, classes containing pointers, pointer to objects, this pointer, array of objects, standard C++ string class, member functions, string modifiers, differences between pointers and references, multidimensional arrays (inside main and inside class), pointer to data member [[cite:8ad84b89037231bb]].

- Constructors, Destructors and File Handling: Manager functions (constructors and destructors), default constructor, constructor with default arguments, destructors, parameterized constructor, copy constructor, initializer lists [[cite:be775cdccf11f750]].

- Data File operations: Opening and closing of files, modes of file, file stream functions, reading/writing of files, sequential and random access file processing, binary file operations, classes and file operations, structures and file operations [[cite:be775cdccf11f750]].

- Operator Overloading and Type Conversion: Operator overloading (unary and binary), type conversions (basic type to class type, class type to basic type) [[cite:be775cdccf11f750]].

- Inheritance: Inheritance basics (derived and base classes), types (simple, multi-level, multiple, hierarchical), modes (private, protected, public), overriding member functions, order of execution of constructors and destructors, resolving ambiguities in inheritance, virtual base class, aggregation and composition [[cite:be775cdccf11f750]].

- Dynamic Memory Management and Polymorphism: Dynamic memory allocation using new and delete operators, virtual destructors, compile and runtime polymorphism, virtual functions, dynamic constructors, abstract classes and concrete classes, self-referential classes, pure virtual functions, early binding and late binding, memory leaks and allocation failures [[cite:be775cdccf11f750]].

- Exception Handling, Templates and Standard Template Library (STL): Basics of exception handling, throwing and catching mechanisms, rethrowing exceptions, function and class templates, class templates with inheritance, introduction to STL containers, algorithms, and iterators, container types such as vector and list [[cite:695bb51bc95d23ba]].

These topics are structured across Units I to VI in the syllabus [[cite:0e8460c617cce338]].
